exposure: Gut microbiome colonization by the same bacterial strain causing subsequent bloodstream infection
Relative abundance of causative bacterial species in the gut
cohort: The study included 19 infants with bacterial bloodstream infection (BSI) and 37 controls, hospitalized in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs), paired for gestational age, days of life, antibiotic exposure, delivery mode, and sex.
finding: Infants who experience a bloodstream infection possess significantly higher median relative abundances of the causative bacterial species in their gut relative to paired controls in the 2 weeks prior to bacteremia.
gest_age: Infants were paired for gestational age, though specific ages are not provided.
